rules.explanation: Learning technologies randomly without identifying core prerequisites leads to surface-level knowledge and slow career progression.
rules.do: Audit current technical competencies against target role roadmaps, prioritizing foundational skills before advanced domain frameworks.
rules.dont: Do not jump into high-level abstractions or advanced tools without solid mastery of core computer science fundamentals.

rules.explanation: Being an absolute generalist with no depth or a narrow specialist who cannot collaborate across domains limits long-term career growth.
rules.do: Cultivate a 'T-Shaped' profile: deep expertise in one primary discipline (vertical) with broad working knowledge of related fields (horizontal).
rules.dont: Do not remain purely superficial across dozens of tools without achieving production-grade depth in at least one core domain.

rules.rule_name: Continuous Milestone Tracking and Evidence-Based Learning
rules.explanation: Setting vague learning targets ('learn cloud') without concrete milestone outcomes results in lack of accountability and lost momentum.
rules.do: Set SMART learning goals linked directly to verifiable proof-of-work output (e.g., build and deploy a microservice by end of month).
rules.dont: Do not measure learning progress merely by tutorial consumption hours rather than functional project execution.

rules.rule_name: Adaptability to Industry Shifts and Emerging Stacks
rules.explanation: Rigid adherence to declining legacy tools without tracking market shifts leads to technical obsolescence and reduced career mobility.
rules.do: Monitor quarterly industry demand trends and proactively integrate high-value emerging standards (e.g., GenAI APIs, Cloud Native) into your stack.
rules.dont: Do not ignore market shifts or resist adopting modern industry standard tools within your core domain.
